hints.title: Bidirectional Call Symmetries
hints.text: Calls between person A and person B can be recorded with from_id = A and to_id = B, or vice versa.

hints.title: Canonicalizing Person Pairs
hints.text: normalize the pair by choosing the minimum id as person1 and maximum id as person2.

hints.title: Aggregating Duration and Count
hints.text: group by person1 and person2, then aggregate with count and sum of duration.

hints.title: Complete Implementation
hints.text:
```mysql
SELECT LEAST(from_id, to_id) AS person1,
       GREATEST(from_id, to_id) AS person2,
       COUNT(*) AS call_count,
       SUM(duration) AS total_duration
FROM Calls
GROUP BY person1, person2;
```

complexity.notes: LEAST and GREATEST canonicalize caller pairs for single-pass hash grouping.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Grouping on raw from_id and to_id separates calls made in opposite directions into different groups.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Evaluating LEAST and GREATEST per row takes O(1) time and allows single-pass hash grouping in linear time.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Candidate should use LEAST/GREATEST or a CASE statement to canonicalize unordered pairs.

solutions.code:
import pandas as pd
import numpy as np

def number_of_calls(calls: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    calls['person1'] = np.minimum(calls['from_id'], calls['to_id'])
    calls['person2'] = np.maximum(calls['from_id'], calls['to_id'])
    res = calls.groupby(['person1', 'person2']).agg(
        call_count=('duration', 'count'),
        total_duration=('duration', 'sum')
    ).reset_index()
    return res
